title: Taquería Luna Comal — a before/after website makeover
description: A before/after makeover for an invented Houston East End taquería. The 2009 site has Comic Sans at 10 px, a phone number and a menu that are only pictures, a 4.8 MB hero (simulated), no hours and no mobile layout. It sits in a scaled frame, so the page itself never scrolls sideways. The mobile-first rebuild has tap-to-call, a live open/closed badge worked out in US Central time, a real text menu, a pickup-order form, sample reviews marked as such, an FAQ and Restaurant JSON-LD. A 'What changed' panel highlights each fix in the frames, and a scorecard runs 11 in-page checks (not Lighthouse) on both versions.
prompt: Make a before/after website makeover for a fictional Houston taqueria (invent the name) as proof for my $1,200 Landing Page, Built + Tested package. The before should be a believable dated small-business site: tiny low-contrast text, no call to action, the phone number and the menu as images without alt text, a huge slow hero (simulated), no hours, no meta description and no mobile layout, shown in a scaled frame so the page never scrolls sideways. The after should be modern, fast, accessible and mobile-first, with tap-to-call, hours with open/closed-now in Central time via Intl, a map-free location block, a clear order CTA, sample reviews that are labelled as samples, an FAQ and Restaurant JSON-LD. Add a keyboard-accessible before/after toggle, a 'What changed' panel linked to highlighted areas, and a live scorecard from in-page checks that is clearly not Lighthouse. Link the CTA to my services section and say in the footer that it's a fictional business.

methodology: Independent oracle for the scorecard: the spec collects raw computed styles, rects and head tags from each frame, then judges all 11 checks in Node with its own WCAG luminance code (sRGB 0.04045 threshold, where the page uses 0.03928). It compares every check's pass flag and its counts (failing elements, totals, heading order, h1 count, JSON-LD type, body font size) with the page's data attributes, for both versions, and again after switching between the phone and desktop widths.

The contrast formula is checked against published reference values first (black on white is 21:1, #767676 on white is 4.54:1, #777777 falls just under 4.5). Every text element of the new site, FAQ answers opened, must then pass AA.

Open/closed-now under page.clock: 9:59 → 10:00 PM on a Thursday in daylight time is checked in two browser contexts whose own time zones are Pacific/Kiritimati and America/Los_Angeles. An 8 AM Sunday opening, the closed Monday and the 11 PM Saturday close are checked in standard time. Expected strings come from the test's own hours table and the published US DST offsets, not from the page.

JSON-LD is parsed in Node and cross-checked against what's visible: the telephone matches every tel: link, and openingHoursSpecification expanded per day matches the hours table row by row. The markup has no aggregateRating, because the reviews are samples.

Behaviour: the tab toggle driven with Arrow, Home, End and Tab keys; every 'Show on old/new site' button highlights exactly one element and scrolls it into the frame's view; no page overflow at 360 px with the 980 px old site shown in both preview widths; and the demo form sends no requests.
risks: The contrast check reads background-color only. Text over an image or gradient is judged against the colour underneath, so the rebuild keeps all text on solid fills. The page says this under the scorecard.

Both the page and the spec pick 'text elements' the same way (visible elements with their own non-empty text), so a rule they agree on but that is wrong wouldn't be noticed. A mutation that changed the page's font threshold from 12 px to 11 px was caught. Changing the tap threshold from 24 px to 20 px was not, because no element on either site falls between those sizes.
The slow hero is an animation, and the 24-second figure is arithmetic (4.8 MB × 8 ÷ 1.6 Mbps), not a measurement. Both are labelled as simulated.
The frames are srcdoc documents, so their links resolve against the Lab page's URL. The page intercepts every link and form inside them; without that, '#menu' would load the Lab page into the frame.
qa.playwright: frameLocator made the same-origin srcdoc frames easy to reach for text, attributes and labelled form fields, and page.evaluate on each iframe's contentDocument returned the raw facts for the Node-side oracle. page.clock.install followed by pauseAt and runFor(61 s) crossed each boundary deterministically. setSystemTime by itself doesn't fire timers, so each jump is followed by a runFor and the cases were chosen to hold for that whole minute. browser.newContext({ timezoneId }) proved time-zone independence better than test.use would have, because the same instant is checked under two different machine zones in one test. Clicking a tel: link inside a CSS-scaled iframe worked on both projects, which I hadn't been sure of. expect.poll waits for the frames to be ready instead of a fixed timeout. There are no screenshot assertions, so purely visual regressions in either mock site would pass.
coverage: Scorecard vs independent oracle, both versions, both preview widths, and after a form submit adds text
WCAG AA contrast of the whole rebuild, formula reference values
Restaurant JSON-LD vs visible phone and hours; the old site has none
Open/closed-now across CDT and CST boundaries under two machine time zones
Tap-to-call href on every phone link; the old number exists only as an image
Keyboard tabs, no horizontal scroll at 360 px, 'What changed' highlights, services CTA and fiction labels

a11y: The toggle is a WAI-ARIA tablist with a roving tabindex, Arrow, Home and End keys, and a tabpanel labelled by the selected tab. The hidden frame is made inert and invisible. Each frame has a descriptive title, and each fix's buttons have names saying which fix and which site they show. View changes, highlights and the demo dialler are announced through an aria-live region. The scorecard is a real table with row and column headers. In the rebuild, every field has a visible label, buttons and fields are 44 to 52 px tall (every tap target clears the 24 px check), the stylised map has a text alternative, and all text passes WCAG AA by the page's own check.
